utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Madam Registrar. Could you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-05-88-T, The Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic, et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Let's start from here. Good morning, everybody. We are sitting pursuant to rule 15 bis for the time being. Judge Stole will join us later on. Today, accused Nikolic is not with us. We are already in possession of the waiver, so we can proceed in his absence. Prosecution today is represented by Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Thayer. Amongst the Defence teams, I notice the absence of Mr. Bourgon, Mr. Josse. That's it. Mr. Jankovic, good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Welcome back. We will soon be proceeding with your testimony. In the meantime, be patient with us so that I raise two minor matters, which we could resolve very quickly. Let's go into private session for awhile, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Jankovic. I hope you've had an opportunity to have a good rest over the past few days. May we now please continue with your examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On Thursday, we left it off with your departure from Doboj towards Zvornik, and I was going to show you a number of documents that I have prepared for you, so let's do that first. First of all, can we see 1D 4D394 in e-court, please. Can you see the document on the screen, Mr. Jankovic? This is an order by the deputy Minister of the Interior dated 13 July 1995, and the first thing I would like to look at is the list of addressees. You can see in the heading of the document that a reference is made to the special police brigade, the commander, the special branch police station in Doboj, the public security centre in Doboj, the command staff of the police forces of the RS MUP for information and the CJB Zvornik to the chief for information. And further on, it says, "In view of the developments around Srebrenica, I hereby issue the following order: Immediately former reinforced police unit which comprised the 1st Company of the Doboj PJPs and partial forces of the Doboj SAP, which is at the base in Doboj." Further on, it says that "The unit is to report to Zvornik in the course of the day where it will be assigned specific tasks." You had an opportunity to see the document while you were being prepared for the testimony. Can you now tell me, with regard to the contents of the document here, a reference is made to the 1st Company of the Doboj PJP; were you a member of the 1st PJP or some other company.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw the document during the preparations. This is a dispatch by the Ministry of the Interior, pursuant to which I was dispatched to Zvornik. The company number, I don't remember whether it was the 1st or the 5th. I believe that it was the 5th. Maybe here it should read 1 company of the PJP. In any case, I was the 5th company from Doboj, and this is the order pursuant to which I was sent to Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let me just ask you this: When you set out for Zvornik, was this unit of the special detachment of the police in Doboj, did it leave with you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to see them or encounter them either on your way to Zvornik or once you were already there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never saw the special detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any connection or links with them, with the part of the 5th detachment?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. We will no longer need this document, and now I would like us to look at another document. May the Court please produce 4D62. This is another order dated 14 July 1995, which was sent to the Bijeljina CJB. What I'm interested in, again, first of all, who the addressees of the order are. We can actually see in the upper part of the document that the document speaks about the dispatch of the police units which was sent to the SJBs in Brcko, Samac, Lopare, Ugljevik, and Pelagicevo; then to the police stations in Bijeljina and Janja, to the commanders thereof; the traffic safety police station in Bijeljina; the border control police station in Bijeljina; and it says here, also, the communications department of the Bijeljina CJB. According to your information, are all these police stations that were part of the security services centre of Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are public security stations and police stations from the territory of Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And now let's look at bullet point 4. Can this please be zoomed in on the screen. It says here, "On arrival in the CJB Zvornik, the unit commander is duty-bound to report to the command staff of the centre who will assign him with the specific tasks." I'm asking you this just to learn about the principle of the special police forces. Was your unit dispatched in the same way as is indicated in this document? I.e., were you instructed to report to the security services centre in Zvornik were you were would be assigned specific task?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was the principle, and this was how special police units were dispatched.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And let's now look at the bullet point 5 of this order. "PJP members should be supplied with two combat kits, ammunition, and the other equipment, which is necessary for the field mission, and attire them in green camouflage uniform." Is that the same thing that you had? Was that the same uniform that you had?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's how we were sent, and this is exactly the equipment and -- that we had on us. We had our personal weapons and combat kit and the green camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. We will no longer need this document. Thank you. When you left Modrica, before your departure, were you told where you were going?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were only told that we were supposed to go to Zvornik where we should report to the security services centre and await a further instructions that would come from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you did not know concretely what your mission would be when you left?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not have any concrete information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me when you arrived in Zvornik, approximately?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We arrived sometime in the afternoon, or rather, late afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me whether the buses stopped on the way.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bus stopped close to the passenger bridge leading to Serbia, i.e., on the border crossing for pedestrians.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. What happened next? The bus pulled over. What happened next? Did you all stay here? Did somebody leave?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Gavric got off the first bus and went to the security services centre, and the rest of us remained on -- sitting on the buses. A few got out to light a cigarette.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And after awhile, did your company commander, Mr. Gavric, return?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Gavric returned within half an hour, maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And can you please tell me whether he told you where he had been, who he had been with, what he had done there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Just briefly, he told us that he went -- had gone to the centre to talk to the deputy whose name, I believe, was Mane, and then he told us that the buses should be on their way to the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Did he tell you then what your mission and tasks would be?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at the time. Nothing concretely.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What happened next? Did the buses continue? Did they go anywhere?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we went to a building which I believe was the Standard barracks, and then a soldier got on the first bus together with Gavric, and then the buses continued. I don't know where they went, but they took an asphalt road, and then we reached a narrow macadam road, and the buses could not negotiate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And just a few additional questions. You said that Gavric had arrived with another soldier. Were they on the same bus? Did they get on the same bus where you were, or --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Gavric and that soldier were on the first bus, and I was on the second bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you did not have an opportunity to hear what they were saying or communicate with them?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And now can you please continue. You arrived at the macadam road. What happened next?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We got off the buses, and then on foot we proceeded along a dirt path, which was leading towards a hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Could you just approximately tell us what time of day it was when you arrived at your destination?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was night. It was already rather dark. It was after nightfall, and I remember that we passed by a repeater. I remember that vaguely.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would like us to look at another document. Could the Court please produce P377. This is the -- page 132. I believe that it is the same page in the English version. This is the logbook of the duty operations officer of the Zvornik Brigade. Could we please scroll down to the bottom part of the document for the witness's benefit. I would like to show the witness the last entry on this page. Mr. Jankovic, in this logbook we have an entry indicating the time 2000 hours, and after that you can see CJB-Mane, one unit of 100 soldiers arriving. You've already told us that there was a deputy chief of the CJB under the name of Mane, and it says one unit of 100 soldiers arriving. Would that approximately tally with the number of yours who arrived with the 5th company?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That could be that. There were 100 or around 100 of us and here, CJB Mane, I suppose that that's that. That's what I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. We will no longer need this document. Thank you. And this may be a good point for me to ask you this: At the time, in July 1995, did you know Mr. Ljubomir Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And this entire period from the moment you left from Modrica, came to Zvornik - I'm going a little bit ahead - and were a participant in certain actions and after that were captured, did you at any point have the opportunity or the possibility to see Mr. Ljubomir Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't see Mr. Borovcanin at all. I just heard that such a person existed, but I never met him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You told us that you reached the end of the asphalt road and then went along on the macadam road. Can you please tell us what date this is? Is this the night of the 13th and 14th? Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the 13th in the evening, so it's the night between the 13th and 14th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can you please tell me if you found out what the name of that sector was called, where you arrived and where you left the bus? Do you remember the name of the village? If you can remember.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The village we reached was called Maricici. I found that out later. At that moment, I didn't know that. I didn't have information about the place that we had reached.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. When you left the bus and set off, did anybody deploy your unit? Did anyone tell you what to do, what you will continue to do?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no concrete assignments that night. In the course of the night, we came to that village. We stationed ourselves in a wood. We were all tired. We were resting there. We didn't have any concrete tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let me just ask you one more question about this. You already told us that you were issued with communication means. Were you personally issued with such means when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The communication devices were issued to me on the 14th in the morning when it got light. I didn't have any communication devices during the night. I got them from the company commander Gavric.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us now move to the morning of the 14th of July. Can you please tell us what was happening in the morning of the 14th?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the morning on the 14th, we made coffee, had breakfast; we were relaxed in this wood perhaps until almost noon when I got information that I was supposed to go to a meeting with Gavric.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And did you go to the meeting? Who else was present? What was discussed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did went to the meeting with Gavric. Another two platoon commanders were there, myself, Gavric, and a member of the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, what was the topic of the meeting? What did you talk about? Did you get any concrete assignments at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They explained to us -- Gavric explained to us where we were, that location, and he told us what our assignment was; or rather, he said that we had to get to Snagovo to some asphalt road where together with the Army of Republika Srpska we would set up a line that would be there in order to prevent a possible breakthrough of the Muslim forces into the town of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And after that, did you go to carry out these assignments?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that, we returned to our units, and I personally conveyed to the other unit members what our task was. We prepared to move out.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. So can you please tell us how things proceeded. You set out to establish that line, as you said. Can you please tell us how events unfolded after that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometime in the afternoon, perhaps around 3.00 p.m., we set off in the direction of Snagovo. First, we passed through a large forest; later, we crossed a meadow.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just one question before you go on. Tell me, if to the right of your unit there was any other unit, were you in touch with them? Can you please explain this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the right, there was a military formation. I don't know exactly which formation, whether it was a platoon or a company. I had personal contact with the commander of that formation. We moved together. They also were moving towards Snagovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's clarify. When you say you had personal contact, can you explain what that specifically means? Did you stand next to him, or did you have visual contact? Can you please explain this to us?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we left Maricici, we had personal contact. We were a metre away from each other. But later, we had visual contact; and after a certain period of time, we couldn't see each other any more. We could hear each other [as interpreted]. We were not linked in in the network.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just one correction for the transcript. On page 12, it says "We could hear each other." This is line 8 and 9, but you said that you could not hear each other. This is just something that I would like to correct.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We could not hear each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. So you told us that you passed through a forest and that you reached a meadow. Can you tell me how things proceeded from there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We crossed this meadow, and we reached a brook, and there was another forest in front of this brook or creek. We stopped there briefly. I spoke with my men, told them that I didn't have anymore contact with the soldiers. After that, I heard a strong -- a loud detonation to the left from the place where I was standing; and after that, I could hear infantry weapons fire. Evidently battle had commenced, and it was getting closer to me. After 15 minutes, we were also exposed to fire, and we had a fire and attack immediately in front of us. Bombs were falling. Bullets were also whizzing around us above our heads.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Very well. Can you tell us what happened then, who was with you, and how this attack continued? And of course, you can explain to us in your testimony what happened then.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We tried to return fire, but it was useless in view of the position where we were. We were in a creek, and in front of us there was an incline and a forest. I could see that the whole unit was in danger. We had one man who was wounded, and I decided to try to pull out the unit from that ambush. I took three of my companions, members of my platoon, and first went to the right and then forward along the incline or the slope. I moved 1 or 200 metres, perhaps, but I couldn't observe the Muslims, and we were still under fire. We were in an ambush, caught in the fire. I told my companions to find some kind of shelter or shield, and then I went by myself some 50 metres forward to see what was going on, to see which forces were attacking us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us if at one point you were captured and how this came about?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At one point, I was among a group of Muslim soldiers who were well camouflaged and concealed, and I was literally captured; I was caught. After that, I disarmed and they took me some 100 metres farther forward to a hillock. The whole situation was being observed by a member of my platoon, but I gave him a sign at one point not to make any moves because I knew that that would mean the end of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can you tell us, after that moment when you were captured, where you were taken?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was taken to a hillock not far from there, and a member of the Muslim army placed his foot on my head, took out a knife, which he placed on my neck, and then he gave my Motorola to me, and he handed it to me and told me to call my commander to immediately stop firing, which I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me what happened then, after you called your commander? Of course, you are talking about Gavric; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I only had a connection with Gavric and the commanders of the other two platoons. I called Gavric and asked him to do what the member of the Muslim army said, but I said that nine of my colleagues were also captured with me, which was not true. I was the only one who was captured. I said that they would kill me if they continued to fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And now, can you please tell me if the fire stopped after you called Commander Gavric?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The firing didn't stop immediately. It stopped a little bit later. The news spread fast that I was captured, and some commanders and commandeers of the Muslim army began to arrive. Some said I should be killed. Some said I should be left alive, that I was valuable, and they decided to take me with them. Again, I mentioned that once I came to the hillock, I was surprised by the fact that I saw with my very own eyes at least 5 to 6.000 people. I saw an enormous column that was in front of me, both to the left and to the right of me, and it was moving. It was independent of the unit that had captured me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would just -- well, excuse me. I don't want to interrupt your testimony, but I would just like to put some questions to you about this column that you saw, and you gave us the number that you estimate of people who were in the column. Was the column made up only of men, or did you notice any details? Were there any women or children?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that there were no children in the column. At least, I didn't see any. There were some women, not many. The column mainly included middle-aged men, and there were also some elderly men.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us, these men that you were able to see in the column, were they armed; and are you able to tell us to what extent they were armed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were armed. In my estimate, 80 percent of them carried weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And can you please tell me, were you able to notice the part of the column where you were, the part of the column that you were able to see, were the men in that part of the column wearing uniforms?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was everything. There were complete uniforms, parts of uniforms. There were also civilians. It was a mixture.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When you say there were civilians, were you able to see if those people in civilian clothing also were armed or not? Can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were armed people. A number of them were armed. There were some people who had hunting rifles or semi-automatic rifles of an older type.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can you please tell me if at one point you continued to move in the column?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The column kept moving the whole time. It didn't stop. Not even at the point in time when I was captured, the column did not stop. I was captured by the flank security of the column. The column was moving in a formation. It had its flank security, forward security, rear scouts. It was an orderly formation, and that's how the column moved. All the prominent people from Srebrenica were in the column.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Who did you see of the Srebrenica leadership or the military commanders of the 28th Division? Who did you see personally? Can you remember? Could you please tell us?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally saw Zulfo Tursunovic, and I also saw the commander of the 28th Division whose name I don't know. I only know that he had replaced Naser Oric who had fled Srebrenica before Srebrenica fell.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All that time, were you in the same part of the column, or did it come a time when you came closer to the front of the column or when you found yourself closer to the middle of the column? Can you please be more specific and give us some detail?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was mostly in the middle of the column or closer to its front. I never moved back to the rear, and this is also where the command was within the first third of the column.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You've already told us that Zulfo Tursunovic was there. Could you please describe the event when you came close to Zulfo Tursunovic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had a personal contact with him. The members of the military that captured me brought me to Tursunovic and ordered me to kneel in front of him. He was sitting on a horse. He was mounted on a horse, and he asked me about my personal details, what my name was, where I was from. He also asked me what unit I belonged to. And then he told me, Very well, my son, I won't kill you; I need you alive. And then I was taken away from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And you have also told us about how the column advanced. Did you have an impression that it was a combat column, organised column, or was it a chaotic formation that was moving in a rather unorganized way?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I already told you, in my view the column was well organised. There was nothing chaotic about that. They had scouts, leaders, guides, people who were familiar with the terrain. And they also had elite units that protected the unit, the column, in my view that had been composed of the youngest and most capable men. At least, that's the way I saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You've already told us that you had an opportunity to see that a large number of the men in the column were armed. What kind of weapons did you notice among the members of the BiH Army who were in the column?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally was astonished when I saw their weaponry. Let me just give you an example of the kind of weapons that I had never saw in our police or our military. Those were rifles with nitroglycerin bullets and they also had machine -- two 12.7 machine guns, Browning -- Brownings, sniper rifles, 84-millimetre machine guns. Their weapons were really good. They were really well armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In addition to the infantry weapons that you just mentioned as having had an opportunity to see, did you have any artillery pieces among the soldiers that were moving in the column?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I noticed Brownings that were mounted on horses, and I also noticed anti-helicopter rockets known as "strijela" or arrows.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you also have an opportunity to see among the soldiers who were moving with the column some signals means, communications means? Did they have that as well?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They had very good communication means, which were also mounted on horses. I saw huge batteries that they were carrying and big antennas. I believe that they had some military communications means that I'd never seen before, so I wouldn't be able to tell you what they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And while you were moving with the column, did you have an occasion to hear any conversations among the soldiers in the column? What were they talking about? What was the topic of their discussions there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I could hear conversations amongst the people who were in the column. They mostly talked about the way they would cross into the free territory in the Tuzla region, and they had certain contacts with the command of the Army of Republika Srpska with this regard. They mentioned me as their possible victim or a chip-in for exchange.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, you are all aware that we started almost 40 minutes late today because of --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Your Honour. This is why I want to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- a technical problem that we had which couldn't be resolved earlier. We've discussed amongst ourselves how best to proceed. Our suggestion is that the break will be at 10.40, in other words, in about 15 -- almost 15 minutes from now, and it will be reduced to 20 minutes, so we try to regain a little bit of what we lost. And the next break will also be of 20 minutes. So we'll have a break at 10.40, and we'll resume at 11.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, for this guidance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jankovic, my next question is this: Did all the people in the column share the same point of view as to whether to proceed, whether to go back, whether to keep on moving? Did you have an occasion to hear any of their opinion with this regard?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had a lot of opportunity to hear that. Their positions were not unique. They were split. Even in the command, there were people who did not agree with the commander's decisions. Some wanted to kidnap me and surrender together with me. There were even such stories -- there was a lot of confusion among them, and they were not united. They were, rather, divided. They did not have a united front.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you have an occasion to hear or see some situations when people committed suicide or when there was an internal showdown among the people moving the column?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally witnessed only one such case, and I heard from my guards that there had been a number of such situations where people had killed each other. There were even such situations that a father shot a son or a brother shot at a brother, and I said on occasion to see on the 15th when a soldier had activated a hand grenade which killed him and another man and wounded four or five other men.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. In addition to the contact that you already described for us with Commander Gavric using a Motorola, were you asked later on during your advancement to re-establish the contact with somebody using a Motorola?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did ask me to do that. I don't know who my contact was, but I know that I did; and every time I talked to somebody, I heard on the side of the Army of Republika Srpska that possibilities were sought for the corridor to be opened and for the column to be let through in the desired direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And did you personally communicate with somebody, or was the communication established using a Motorola?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think my Motorola was used. I think it was done using other communications means.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Give me a general picture of the relationship or attitude of the BiH Army members towards you from the moment you were captured during the time when you moved with the column?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was rather volatile. At one point, I had an impression that I was a very important person. I was a privileged person, well protected, and I did not suffer any unpleasant situations; and this lasted up to the moment when we crossed the separation line close to the village of Nezuk.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. We will come to that moment in a minute, but now I just wanted to see in more general terms whether your personal effects had been taken from you, and if they were, what was taken from you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All my personal effects were taken away from me. They even took off my boots, and the last thing that they took from me was my gold ring, and this was a counter favour for them having put a bandage on my head.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And while you were moving with the column, did you receive any food, any water?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And what was the situation in the column when it comes to food and water in more general terms?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that the situation was really bad. They did not have any food. They mostly ate fruit and forest berries. They had some water, which they had obtained from the streams and brooks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And as you were moving with the column on the 14th, 15th and 16th of July, can you remember the places that you passed through?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with the terrain. However, I learned from the conversations that were taking place in the column that we had across the road Zvornik Caparde and that we also crossed over Crni Vrh, and I know that I heard them saying that we had crossed the village of Baljkovica as we were approaching the village of Nezuk.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And can you please tell me when, approximately following the chronology and the dates, when was it that you arrived in the village of Baljkovica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on the 16th of July, sometime in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And now tell me, how did you spend your nights? For example, the night between the 14th and the 15th of July?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We kept on moving during the night. They actually made sure that they moved less during the day and more during the night. I know that the hardest night was between the 15th and the 16th of July. It was raining and there was hail. Actually, there was a storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And -- very well. We come to the 16th. Can you please tell us what happened when you arrived near Baljkovica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the night on the 15th, I heard a conversation - actually, I overheard a conversation - over the radio. Somebody from the Army Republika Srpska asked for the main body of the column to wait for a smaller part of the column to arrive from the Caparde sector. They were supposed to cross the open line on the following day when they would be allowed passage. However, this created a dilemma among the members of the command of the column. There were some who thought that this was a trap, and the others believed the story. I also heard that there was a fire opened because of that among them. However, the final decision of the command was to attempt the breakthrough immediately despite of the promise that the corridor would be open the following day, and this is what was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Could you please describe the events that unfolded on the 16th when you passed Baljkovica, and what happened next?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already told you that they --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Could you give us just a brief outline because I have other things that I would like to move on.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They decided to attempt a breakthrough despite the promises they'd had heard from the Army of Republika Srpska. Units were established that were supposed to attempt the breakthrough. The fighting started in the morning, and at one point I heard them shouting and celebrating, and they said that the road towards Nezuk was open. They took me with them. I passed through Baljkovica across the trenches that had been abandoned, and we crossed over to the territory around the village of Nezuk.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just one more question before the break. When was it, at what time when you arrived in Nezuk according to your best recollection?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was around 1800 hours on the 16th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is an appropriate time to take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. The break, as I said, will be of 20 minutes duration. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jankovic, it's probably my mistake, but I just would like to correct this. At one point, I showed you the duty operations officer notebook of the Zvornik Brigade --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the number of the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: -- and I asked you if you knew -- P377, page 132, where you saw Mane from the Zvornik centre of public security. I just wanted to say when I rechecked it, this is an entry for the 14th, so that was the day when you had already been captured, so we just wanted to clarify that. Thus, that entry cannot refer to your unit, obviously.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. What I wanted to continue with are some video-clips. This is the video material that was disclosed to us by the Prosecution, number V0003676, and this is 4D616. I don't want us to look at the entire clip, which is quite long; I just wanted us to look at three short excerpts on the tape, and these are excerpts beginning from 2 minutes 40 seconds and last until 3.50; then insert beginning at 5.50 to 7.00; and the third insert beginning at 8.20 and beginning [as interpreted] at 10.05. I would like us to look at these three video clips first, and then I will put my questions to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is what we wanted to show. Mr. Jankovic, during proofing for your testimony, you had the opportunity to look at these video clips. Can you please tell me if you recognise where this was actually filmed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was recorded in Nezuk. I recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me if you had the opportunity to recognise anything else that would correspond with your experience relating to the column, anything specific such as trenches, cross trenches or anything that you had had the opportunity to see?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the route that I had passed. You can see that the trenches are abandoned. I noticed, for example, that you don't see anywhere any killed or wounded persons, and you can also see here what I said, and that is that there are no children in the column and that there are very few women. You can also see the weapons that the people in the column had. You were able to see here, a soldier had a rocket. They had machine guns, automatic rifles, bullet cartridges. Some of them had not such good rifles, like hunting rifles or semi-automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Of course, we had the possibility to see there were a large number of persons here in civilian clothing, but they carried weapons. Can you please tell me if this was something that frequently was the case in the column?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You could see in the footage. I saw it, too, when I was in the column. I think that there were quite a lot of such cases where people were wearing civilian clothing and carried weapons, or they perhaps wore a piece of uniform, the shirt or the waistcoat or the trousers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. We didn't have sound. We had technical problems, but you can hear throughout firing, though. Were you able as you were passing to hear firing; and if you did, can you please tell us what that is all about?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was passing in that area, there was no firing in the sense of combat. There was only firing into the air by those people who were probably celebrating the fact that they had crossed to Nezuk territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Unfortunately, we don't have a transcript for this clip, but we will provide it so that we could hear what was actually going on here. That is one of the duties of the Defence to provide that, and we are going to do that. All right. So you were taken to Nezuk. Can you please tell us what happened to you, then, once you crossed these trenches.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was crossing the lines where the trenches were, as I mentioned, they started to physically abuse me. They beat me with all kinds of things. A man beat me with crutches, one with a rifle. Another one used his feet and hands, and I sustained a lot of head injuries, also injuries on other parts of my body. I was beaten all over.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me where you were taken when you got to Nezuk?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was held at a checkpoint of the military police. Actually, it was the first military police checkpoint. I was put into some kind of shed, and I recognised a man there who went to school with me in Sarajevo. His name is Redjo Mesanovic from Srebrenica who worked as a policeman in Bratunac. He took my particulars, and he also said that he recognised me, and I spent about an hour there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me, other than yourself, were there any other Serb prisoners in Nezuk?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was a certain Milan Tesic with me in the same shed. He's from the Zvornik area. He was a member of the Army of Republika Srpska. He was also pretty much beaten. His face was bloody. He kept saying that he was a cook, and they kept beating him, asking him to confess that he was in some artillery outfit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Once you came to Nezuk, were there any attempts to exchange you, and if so, can you please describe when this was and what happened?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They took me to a garage in the village of Nezuk from this shed. And then Semso Muminovic [phoen] arrived, and he said that I would be exchanged on the same day, that same day. Allegedly he had agreed to do that together with Mr. Vinko Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And were you exchanged?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't exchanged that day. I was taken from the garage -- actually, Tesic was taken from the garage, and I didn't see him anymore. After I was exchanged, my brother told me that he had followed Tesic's trail and that he had found him and he had been exchanged, but only a day or two after that I was handed over to a certain Foco who continued with me that day and the whole night. I spent that time in Nezuk, and that was the first time since I was captured that I was given a little bit of food and water.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Do you know of any attempts by the Serbian side to organise your exchange? Were you informed about there having been such attempts?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was informed about it. On the 17th in the morning, I was held in a cellar of a house. Most probably members of the B & H Army from Srebrenica came there, and on several occasions they physically mistreated me, and I -- and inflicted serious bodily wounds on me. Later Foco came, and he said that my troubles were at an end and that I would be freed that evening at 6.00. However, this did not happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would like to look at a document now relating to attempts to exchange you for other detainees. Can we look at 4D552, please. You've had the opportunity to see the document during your proofing, and it says, Re: Zoran Jankovic, information about his arrest sent from the Doboj public security centre -- actually, from the Doboj public security centre traffic safety police station, Modrica. You can see your name, and you can see the date, 2nd of August, 1995, there. I would like us to look at the last two paragraphs, please. At the top, your particulars are referred to and information about when you were captured and the last time you communicated, and that was on the 17th of July around 1800 hours in the village of Nezuk. And you can see that the information about you has been furnished to the exchange commission of the Krajina Corps in Banja Luka, and there is a request to ask the exchange commission through the MUP at the level of the RS MUP for the purpose of releasing and exchanging policeman Zoran Jankovic. Now that we've seen this document, can you please explain if your exchange actually materialized in this period?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The document confirms what I said, that on the 17th of July, around 1800 hours I was taken to the separation line by Foco to be allegedly released. However, I was brought back for reasons unknown to me, and the exchange did not take place.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I would now like in the briefest possible way to hear what happened to you from the moment you crossed into Nezuk. Can you just tell us how long you spent in different detention centres?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the exchange attempt fell through, I was taken to Sapna where I spent the night. Then during the night, an attack was carried out by the Sapna intervention platoon to the place where I was captured. I found this out from Redjo Mesanovic. They wanted to kill me. The following day, Redjo transferred me to what was, according to him, a safe location, and in the afternoon then to Zivinice, to the military police command in Zivinice. That's where I spent a few hours, and then they took me to the Djordjevik [phoen] mine, those policemen, and that's where they locked me up. I was locked up in that mine for 15 days. At one -- I was located in a room with metal doors, and it looked like a solitary confinement cell. So I fell very -- gravely ill there. All my wounds got infected. I was just given two pills for medicine. During that time, I was taken to a place by the commander of the military police, a certain Kabasi, so that I could speak with Mr. Pandurevic via the radio to convince him that I was alive or assure him that I was alive. I spent 15 days in Djordjevik, and when I was found by the ICRC team, or actually, was on its way to discover me, that same person, Amo Kabasi, took me to a different location, to the village of Kovaci to the football stadium to a changing room, and this was before the ICRC team managed to find me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me how long you spent in this changing room of the stadium in Kovaci?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spent about a month there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And then what happened? Were you transferred somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In late August, I was transferred to the barracks Husinska Buna in Tuzla where I was held in military detention. There were three solitary confinement cells of 1 by 2 metres. I was locked up in one of them, and I spent two months there in that cell.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: After that, were you transferred somewhere else? Just tell us where and the period.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was transferred to the town at the -- to the military police command of some 5th detachment of the military police. This was in January. I spent 21 days in the cellar of that building, after which I was returned to the barracks. This was sometime in February. After two days, I was transferred to the central jail, and then in late February 1996, I was registered by the International Committee of the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And during that entire period of your captivity, were you interrogated? Did you have that kind of questioning by various organs of the B & H Army or police?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was some interrogation, but I was never officially interrogated because I was not officially recorded as a prisoner. They could have killed me. I wasn't registered anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And during that time when you were interrogated, did you sign any kind of statement, or were you able to read back what they possibly wrote down?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I can recall, I didn't sign any statement. There were some interviews, but there was no official statement, and even if they did take a statement, I was not able to read what it said in the statement, and I didn't sign any statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jankovic, we showed you two official notes during your preparations for this testimony. We had received those from the Prosecutor's Office, and they concerned the interviews with you. You had an opportunity to review the notes. What are your comments? Is this what you said? Does this contain information that you provided?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw the official notes. One was compiled by the military security and the other by the civilian security. I believe that these were only the results of the work of some operatives in these services who made their notes. I also made similar notes in my service, and these notes contain my personal data and some other things that are correct, but there's also a lot of information that they based on their operative work or their personal information that have not much to do with me. This is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let me just ask you, the official notes that we're talking about, you did not have an occasion to see them before the Borovcanin Defence counsel showed them to you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I never saw them. These are not my statements. They are just official notes, and even on top of that, the official note that was compiled by the military security services, I believe that it is totally false. It says there that a statement was taken from me on the 17th at 10.00. At that time I was in Nezuk in the cellar, and at that particular time I was being beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And now could you please tell me, how much time did you spend in captivity in total, and when were you released?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The total days spent in captivity were 850 -- 252 days, 8 and a half months. I was set free on the 24th March, 1996, in the sector of Doboj municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: As a result of your captivity and the ill treatment that you were subject to, did you suffer any consequences? Did your health suffer?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course my health suffered greatly. As a result, I'm currently a retired policeman, and I have certain health problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I'm not going to insist on you telling us any more detail of that. I have just a few more questions. Did you have an occasion to meet Mr. Ljubomir Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I first saw Mr. Ljubomir Borovcanin when he came to visit me in my house, in my apartment on behalf of the Republika Srpska MUP after the exchange in late March 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Borovcanin represented the MUP and came to visit you. Can you give us some detail of that encounter with Mr. Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He arrived with another colleague from the MUP, and with my commander they came to see me, to see how I was doing and what I looked like, whether I was in need of something after the ordeal I'd been through. We sat down in my apartment, and we had an informal conversation with a cup of coffee and a glass of juice.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And after that, did you have an occasion to see Mr. Borovcanin again?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw him again in the MUP building in Bijeljina when I came to Bijeljina. I visited Mr. Borovcanin and some other people whom I knew there from before.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And in addition to the two encounters that you have just described for us, did you have any other encounters with Mr. Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Only these two. No others.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Jankovic. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zivanovic, do you have any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Your Honour. Just some qualifications.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jankovic, first of all, good morning. Let me introduce myself. My name is Dragan Krgovic, and I represent General Milan Gvero. I'll have some questions for you. In answering my learned friend's questions, you answered a type of weaponry that the Muslims in the column had. You mentioned a heavy machine gun, Browning. Is that an anti-aircraft machine gun?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a machine gun that can be used in anti-aircraft Defence, but it can also be used as an anti-infantry weapon. It has a large calibre, 12.7 millimetre. This is a machine gun that you can, indeed, use in anti-aircraft defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And it is mounted so that it's barrel can be directed vertically?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this machine gun has a metal feet or a metal postument.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Krgovic. Mr. Haynes?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Just a few, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Jankovic. As you know, I represent Vinko Pandurevic. You told us of an event immediately following your capture when you were forced to make a radio call to your commander, Mico Gavric. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that. I remember when I called my commander, Mico Gavric, over the radio.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And during the course of that radio conversation with Mr. Gavric, you told him that there were nine of your unit who were being held captive. That's also correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. I did say that, but it was not nine of my colleagues who were held captive. It was just me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Was it your idea to say that, or were you told to say it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was ordered to say that by this man. I said that my head was on the ground. He put his foot on my head and placed his knife at my throat, and that's when I uttered those words, i.e., I repeated after him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, you've told us about communications between the Muslim forces and the Army of Republika Srpska during the course of the 15th of July. And so that we're clear, that is not communication made via your Motorola radio, is it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. It was not my Motorola radio. I don't know where my Motorola had ended by then.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And how was it that you became aware of those communications? Was that because you were present with the commanders who were making the calls or because those commanders told you what was being negotiated?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there. I was present there, and I even used that same communications means to talk. I believe that they wanted me to confirm that I was still alive, that I was still there, that they wanted to use me as a sort of guarantee.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And your recollection is that by the end of the 15th of July, the position was that the Serbian forces were prepared to let the column walk through to Nezuk but that the Muslim forces did not trust this offer and so did not take it up; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And in particular, the request of the Serbian forces that the column, as it were, bunch up before it walked through to the free territory, was regarded as a trap, rather than as a device to ensure that no stragglers were left behind?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that some of the people in the column really saw it that way, and that was the moment when there were some problems or conflicts among the members of the command of that column as a result of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jankovic. You've brought me on to my next question, which is: Situated, as you were, close to the commanders within the column, your assessment in summary was this, wasn't it, that though it was well armed and in a reasonably good formation, moral within the column was very low, and the commanders were in conflict with one another?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my impression, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Just one more thing. Did you see, during the time that you were with the column, evidence that the column was suffering significant casualties?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did see on a few occasions several dead bodies along the path on which the column was moving.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: During the time that you were with the column, did it ever come under heavy artillery fire?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was no artillery fire on the column while I was with the column. Not for a single moment did I notice or feel a shell falling on the column. I was with the column throughout those two days. On the 16th, there was some shelling but in a distance. Maybe 3 or 4 kilometres away from the column one could hear artillery fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you form the view that that was fire that was coming from Nezuk and the Muslim forces there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was indeed my impression. I believe that that was around the time when we were supposed to cross over to Nezuk or maybe a few hours before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Lastly this: I think when you were crossing the trenches to the free territory, you became aware, firstly, of one solitary dead Serbian soldier; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. There was a stream and --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I interrupted you. Complete your answer.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a stream, and in the stream I saw a dead body lying. The dead body was of a soldier in the camouflage uniform of the Army of Republika Srpska, and the comment I heard from the people who had taken me in, who were leading me, was that they had killed him at that same place.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I think you also saw a further pile of bodies which you concluded were mainly Muslim soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At one point, I saw as many as maybe 50 or so bodies, and I believe that most of them were Muslim soldiers because they did not have complete uniforms, which made them look similar to the people, or rather, soldiers in the column.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Jankovic. I did say to you when we met briefly last week that I didn't think I'd have any questions for you, but I'm sorry to have broken my word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Haynes. Mr. Thayer, we'll have the break at 12.20.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I will conclude my cross before the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. My name is Nelson Thayer, and I'll be asking you some questions on behalf of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I first want to take you back to 14 July when you were heading towards Snagovo with your fellow PJP officers. You told us about a VRS officer who was your neighbour to the right. Now, I know it was 13 years ago, I just want to find out whether as you sit here today you by any chance remember the name of that VRS officer.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. I understand from the proofing note I received from my friends that after reviewing various statements that you gave, you stated that the statement that you gave to the Modrica basic court in June of 1997, you consider to be your most accurate statement of these events; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: There's a reference in the report, and I can show it to you if you need it, but it's a pretty simple question. There's a reference in your report to you seeing a burned ambulance at some point. Do you remember that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember an ambulance. I don't know whether I told you or whether I indeed said that it had been burned. I may have said that it was damaged, but in any case, at the moment when I saw it, it wasn't on fire. I'm sure of that. I said that I had seen the vehicle in the Baljkovica sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And shortly after you referred to this destroyed ambulance in your statement, you refer to Mr. Tesic, and --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I think you referred to him today as Milan Tesic. I'd like to ask you whether you also heard him referred to as Mile or Milos Tesic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what I heard. When we were in the shed and when Redjo asked him what his name was, he said that it was Milan Tesic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. It's not a big point, sir, but if we can just look at 4D 00553 very quickly, page 5 of the original. Sir, if you look in the first paragraph there. I think it's one, two, three, four, five, six, seven lines down, there's a reference to an individual named Tesic in this statement. Do you see that, sir? It's up --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And I just note that here in the statement his name is written down as Mile Tesic. Did they get it wrong in the statement, or do you think your recollection now might be a little bit off about whether it was Milan or Mile Tesic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not a hundred percent sure. It could well be Milo or Milan. It is one in the same in our parts. Maybe his name was Milan and his name -- nickname was Milo or the other way around, but both is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Like I said, it's not a big deal, sir. Did you ever hear that Mr. Tesic had been in that ambulance that was destroyed that you saw? Did you ever hear anything about that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never heard anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And before I get to my last couple of questions, just to clarify one part of your testimony in answer to my friend from the Pandurevic team's questions, you referred - and again, this may have to do with nicknames and so forth - you referred to your PJP company commander as Mico Gavric. I think you testified that his name was Milan Gavric. Are they one in the same to you, or was his name Milan, in fact, and not Mico? Just so the record is clear.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I did not misspoke. The only person who may have misspoken was Mr. Pandurevic's lawyer. I believe I noticed that he said Mico, but actually, it wasn't Mico. It was Milan Gavric.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. You were asked some questions about the efforts to have you exchanged. What efforts were you aware of at the time, or for that matter, have you become aware of since that time to have you exchanged?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question, sir. Are you referring to the period ...

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Other than what you testified to today, some of the conversations you overheard being brought to the line, were you aware at the time that you were being held prisoner, or indeed, have you been made aware after you were released of any efforts to have you exchanged other than what you've already testified about, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, efforts were being made by my family and by my command in Modrica. After all, we had a document in which my commander was calling for my being exchanged. I'm only aware of these efforts, no others.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And I believe you specifically referred to -- or at least the document that you were shown referred to the commission for exchange of POWs, correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the commission is referred to in the document. During the war there were, as a rule, commissions for exchanges of POWs.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: May we have 65 ter 3847 on e-court, and I just have a couple more questions, just two more documents to show you, sir, and a couple of questions. Now, sir, we don't have an English translation of this document, so I'm just going to ask you to take a moment and have a look at it. Take your time.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, my first and family names are mentioned in this document. The command of the Drina Corps is requesting from the commission for exchange to plan a meeting of some sort in the Tuzla district, and I can see here Milan Tanjic or Tanic whom I also mentioned in one of my statements. However, he was not captured at the time. He was captured on the 11th of November, 1995, just as it says in here.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But that's not the same person.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Very well, sir. If we look at the date of this, it's the 27th of December, 1995, and as you said, it's from the command of the Drina Corps, specifically the security organ, and it's addressed to the General Staff of the VRS, the security organ there. Now, I note that in paragraph 1 where it refers to you, sir, there's a reference to the 15th of July. I think we can agree that if that's a reference to the date of your capture, that's off by a day. Can we agree on that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we can say that the difference is only just one day, but as for Tanic or Tesic, there were two men, so the 11th of November would not be that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And as you said, this refers to a planned meeting of the respective POW commissions, and that meeting, as we can see on that very first line of the document, was scheduled for the 28th of December. Is that correct based on what you see here in the document, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible that the meeting was planned for the 28th of December. I was captured on the 14th of July, so that is four and a half months after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: No question about that, sir. If we could just scroll down a little bit into the document. If we look at -- we see the first three prisoners that are referred to, and then there's another set of prisoners. Three Muslims are identified there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And we can see that the signatory on this document is Colonel Vujadin Popovic. Do you know who that is, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if you look at those last two paragraphs before the signature line, sir, he is asking the Main Staff for their -- or for its authorisation and opinion regarding this proposed exchange, this three people for three people; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. If we may have 65 ter 3848, please. And again, sir, we do not have an English translation of this document. I just ask you to take a moment to have a look at it, read it over, and take your time, and let us know when you're ready to move down the document.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if we could just scroll down for the rest of the document, please.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read this as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. If we could just go back, scroll up to the top of the document, and I just have a couple of questions for you. This document is an information reporter -- or a report concerning the work of the RS commission for exchange of POWs. Can we agree on that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if we look at the very first line, it refers to a meeting or negotiations with the Muslim side on the 28th of December; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And again, this document refers to yourself and two other Serb prisoners, Mr. Vukotic and Mr. Tanjic. We can see that in the third paragraph; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My name is mentioned here, yes. Also, the name of Bozo Vukovic and Milomir Tanjic, so we can note that there are these mistakes in the names appearing constantly.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if we could scroll down just a little bit more, sir. Do you see the paragraph that begins with the words -- it looks like "Ponovo su trazili." Sorry for my pronunciation.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that passage. They were asking again for additional information about the missing from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And when you say "they," who are you referring to? Or what does the -- what does that paragraph say? If you could just -- actually, if you could just read that paragraph out into the record, that would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can read it again, but I really don't know who drafted this report. I can read it again. They asked for additional information about the missing from Srebrenica. This time, again, just like the times before, we let them know that the civilian population was evacuated in an organised way to Kladanj and that the fighter forces crossed into Tuzla through the corridor, which they are well aware of, and those who were captured have been deported to the collection centre in Batkovici and exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, my question, sir, is at any time while you were being held by the Muslims, or again, indeed, after your release, did you ever become aware that the fate of the Muslim men and boys from Srebrenica became an obstacle to prisoner exchange negotiations between the two sides, that is, because the VRS would not account for the names of those individuals captured after the fall of Srebrenica? That became an obstacle to the exchange negotiations? Did you ever hear that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not hear that, and I disagree with that. And if I can say something, a couple of words about this. I spent seven months in a solitary confinement cell and was not in a position to know anything about anything, especially anything regarding preparations for my exchange. From the point in time when I was registered by the International Committee of the Red Cross, which was in February 1996, I personally spoke with Mr. Mihail Steiner, and he personally told me that the Serbian side did respect their side and released all the prisoners in all the camps in Republika Srpska and that the Muslims were not holding to their side of the bargain, so we were all being held where we were, and that there were more than 120 of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, my last question is, you told us that your brother had - I believe it was your brother - had in fact encountered Mr. Tesic later on and that he in fact had been released. Can you confirm - and I think this is what you said in your statement - that Mr. Tesic was in fact released, he told your brother that he had been beaten or abused, but then he was subsequently released? Do you stand by that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do stand by that. I stated that and it's true, that my brother was in Zvornik and that he found that gentleman, Mr. Tesic. The only thing that could possibly be is that there were two men; one of them was Tanjic, the other one was Tesic, so we could have had something there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: It's not clear to me, sir. You just said "so we could have had something there." At least that's how it was translated. What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I paused and didn't complete my sentence. Perhaps the last and first names were mixed up because in one of the documents you showed me Tanic. I know this Tanic. He was in Tuzla in prison, but this is a man who was actually captured -- actually, he crossed the line himself when the Dayton Accord was signed in November 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. Well, just so there's no confusion on the record, if we could have 4D 00553 one more time, and let me just show you your statement and see if that helps us sort out whether we're talking about Tanic or Tesic.
